To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mTOR inhibitors are a class of immunosuppresents that have been increasingly used as an alternative to calcineurin inhibitors for solid organ transplantation, and have been associated with lower rates of posttransplant malignancies.

(1) mTOR inhibitors can prevent cancer in transplant recipients; (2) mTOR inhibitors have a role in preventing cancer recurrence in transplant recipients; and (3) the use of mTOR inhibitors in patients with a pre‐existing cancer is safe.

mTOR inhibitors have been shown in vitro and in animal models to inhibit tumor development; mTOR inhibition after solid organ transplant may reduce the risk of malignancy; and mTOR inhibitors may be useful for the treatment of malignancies that are associated with solid organ transplant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic approaches in the field of cancer.
the role of mTOR inhibitors in solid organ transplant recipients with pre‐existing malignancy.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the prevention and treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mTOR inhibition is not yet established as an effective chemoprevention strategy after solid organ transplantation.

mTOR inhibitor‐mediated chemoprevention is a promising strategy for reducing the risk of posttransplant cancer, but that the evidence is currently insufficient to support a definitive recommendation for its use.
the mTOR inhibitor‐related cancer chemoprevention is not a proven concept.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the absence of a prospective randomized trial, it remains unclear whether mTOR inhibitors can reduce cancer risk in solid organ transplant recipients, but it is clear that they can reduce cancer risk.
mTOR inhibition is associated with reduced incidence of de novo malignancies in transplant recipients and is also associated with a reduction of recurrent malignancies.
, in the setting of solid organ transplantation, the mTOR inhibitors sirolimus or everolimus may have an important role to play in the chemoprevention of cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mTOR inhibitors may be useful in the prevention of de novo malignancies after solid organ transplantation.
, although there are no prospective studies to support this, mTOR inhibitors are likely to be safe for use in patients with pretransplant malignancy.
mTOR inhibitor‐mediated cancer prevention is not only possible in principle but may also be clinically relevant.
